title: Temporal Degeneracy Limits Message Passing Decoding of QLDPC Codes Under Repeated Noisy Syndrome Measurements
authors: Dimitris Chytas, Nithin Raveendran, Bane Vasić
abstract: Practical quantum computations can require logical error rates of $10^{-12}$ or lower. Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are promising candidates for reaching such rates with low qubit overhead, provided that their syndromes can be decoded efficiently. Repeated noisy syndrome measurements introduce temporal degeneracy into the space-time decoding graph. We characterize the temporal kernel, whose vectors have zero total data parity, and show that it is generated by elementary temporal codewords of weight $d_v+2$, where $d_v$ is the variable-node degree. For $(d_v,d_c)$-regular parity-check matrices with fixed degrees $d_v,d_c>2$ and girth greater than four, we derive counting bounds and construct degenerate error patterns of weight $(d_v+2)/2$ for even $d_v$ and $d_v+1$ for odd $d_v$, with multiplicity $Θ(nr)$ in the blocklength $n$ and number of measurement rounds $r$. Under the isolation assumption, these patterns cause local failures of deterministic isotropic message-passing decoders under a flooding schedule. These failures depend on the node degrees rather than the minimum distance; for the bivariate bicycle (BB) codes considered, their weight is equal to four. Monte carlo simulations and fixed-weight importance sampling quantify harmful low-weight degenerate error patterns for the min-sum (MS) decoder beyond the isolation assumption. Motivated by the identified symmetries, we propose space-time anisotropic min-sum decoding with syndrome-guided realizations. Its complexity is linear in the number of Tanner graph edges for fixed maximum number of iterations and number of decoders. Numerical results on BB codes show threshold-like behavior acrossthe tested code sizes and improved failure probabilities relative to MS decoding with ordered statistics decoding post-processing.
summary: This paper investigates the performance limits of QLDPC codes when subjected to repeated noisy syndrome measurements, which introduce temporal degeneracy. The authors characterize these degenerate error patterns, showing they cause local failures in standard message-passing decoders. They propose a novel space-time anisotropic decoding technique that overcomes these limitations, demonstrating improved error correction capabilities.
main_problem: The paper analyzes how temporal degeneracy, introduced by repeated noisy syndrome measurements, limits the performance of message-passing decoding for Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (QLDPC) codes.
main_result: It constructs degenerate error patterns whose weight depends only on the node degrees, causing local failures in standard isotropic decoders, and proposes a new anisotropic decoding scheme with improved performance.
method: The authors characterize the temporal kernel, derive counting bounds for degenerate error patterns, and compare the performance of standard min-sum decoding against a novel space-time anisotropic decoding approach.
model_or_system: The study uses QLDPC codes to model quantum error correction (QEC) under a phenomenological noise model involving multiple rounds of noisy syndrome measurements.
key_observables: Logical error rates, weight of degenerate error patterns, failure probabilities of decoders.
important_parameters: Variable-node degree ($d_v$), number of measurement rounds ($r$), blocklength ($n$), and the code's girth.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the isolation assumption and assumes the existence of $(d_v, d_c)$-regular parity-check matrices with girth greater than four.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes mention figures illustrating a symmetric stabilizer and an example of a temporal codeword.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by characterizing the temporal kernel, deriving combinatorial bounds on degenerate error patterns, proving the failure mechanism for isotropic decoders, and concluding with the proposal and simulation of an improved anisotropic decoding algorithm.
why_interesting: While focused on QEC, the analysis of structured failures due to symmetries (degeneracy) and the development of specialized decoding algorithms are highly relevant to understanding the limitations of quantum information processing in noisy environments.
